context.deployment_shape: Mimir 3.1.2, monolithic mode, single replica, ingester.ring.replication_factor already set to 1 (the fix from the previous incident in this series is already applied and confirmed working -- the 'at least 2 live replicas required' error is gone).
context.cluster_scale: This is a single-node home-lab Kubernetes cluster with a modest but real set of scraped services (roughly 20 real Prometheus scrape jobs across application services, infra components, and an eBPF auto-instrumentation DaemonSet with high label cardinality).

symptom.observed_behavior: Most real Prometheus remote_write requests are still being rejected, with a different error than before.
real_log_lines: level=warn method=/cortex.Ingester/Push duration=5.308129ms msg=gRPC err="user=anonymous: per-user series limit of 150000 exceeded (err-mimir-max-series-per-user). To adjust the related per-tenant limit, configure -ingester.max-global-series-per-user, or contact your service administrator. (sampled 1/10)"

level=error user=anonymous msg="detected an error while ingesting Prometheus remote-write request (the request may have been partially ingested)" httpCode=400 err="send data to ingesters: failed pushing to ingester mimir-74b8b445bc-xnj7h: user=anonymous: per-user series limit of 150000 exceeded (err-mimir-max-series-per-user)..."
symptom.real_query_result: curl -s 'http://<real-prometheus>:9090/api/v1/query?query=prometheus_tsdb_head_series' returns a real current value of approximately 186604 active series on this cluster's own Prometheus.

note_to_agent: The replica-count problem from before is confirmed fixed and is not the cause here -- this is a different, new error message. Diagnose the real cause and what you'd change.

reference_answer.root_cause: Mimir's ingester.max-global-series-per-user defaults to 150000 (per-tenant, real default confirmed via the binary's own -help-all output). This cluster's real, measured active series count (prometheus_tsdb_head_series ~186,604) is already above that default cap before Mimir even started deduplicating/ingesting anything of its own -- the default limit was simply undersized for this cluster's real cardinality, not a bug in Mimir or in the deployment shape.
reference_answer.fix_applied: Set limits.max_global_series_per_user: 300000 in the Mimir config -- real headroom above the measured 186,604 figure, not an arbitrarily large number.
reference_answer.verification: After redeploying with the raised limit, real remote_write pushes stopped being rejected for the series-limit reason, and a real query for up{job="beyla"} (and other real jobs) through Mimir's own /prometheus-prefixed query API returned real, current data end to end.
reference_answer.related_but_deliberately_unfixed_finding: A separate, smaller issue was found at the same time and deliberately left unfixed, not silently patched: some series from an OTel Collector's own self-monitoring metrics carry a label literally named 'server.address' (a raw OpenTelemetry semantic-convention attribute name, containing a dot) -- valid enough for Prometheus's own local TSDB to accept without complaint, but rejected by Mimir's own stricter remote-write label-name validation (err-mimir-label-invalid). This is real, deliberate, documented evidence that Mimir's ingest path enforces stricter rules than plain Prometheus at this project's real scale -- not something a fully-correct diagnosis needs to fix, but a strong answer should at least be able to distinguish it from the series-limit issue if given both symptoms together.
